title: Equal-degree fractions in a localized module
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $M$ an $R$-module, $I$ an index set, $A_i\subseteq R$ and $M_i\subseteq M$ families of subsets, and $T\subseteq R$ a multiplicative submonoid. Inside $T^{-1}M$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization], the equal-degree fraction subset is $\{y/h: \exists i\in I,\ y\in M_i,\ h\in T\cap A_i\}$. For graded families these are exactly the homogeneous fractions of degree zero; equality is the ordinary localization equivalence relation. This definition names the subset, with module operations inherited from localization when the families are gradings.
